Official Card Attributes Reference

Every card in the catalog carries official rules attributes synchronized directly from the Cardnum open database. Depending on the attribute, values can be filtered in the lower panel (Slots 1 & 2), queried in procedural deck rules, or inspected in the right-click Card Attributes monospace view.

Illustrative Values Notice: The values listed throughout this reference are representative examples drawn from the seven official Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.) expansion sets (The Wizards, The Dragons, Dark Minions, The Lidless Eye, Against the Shadow, The White Hand, and The Balrog). They are not intended to be exhaustive closed lists. Because Cardnum syncs open community data, you will also encounter specialized traits, set-specific havens (e.g. Wizardhaven), and composite shorthand codes (e.g. B, B F) in the dropdowns.

1. Basic Card Information

These core properties identify each card and provide its gameplay text. They are displayed in the right-click Card Attributes monospace readout or controlled through dedicated application menus, rather than the filter slot dropdowns:

2. Official Gameplay Attributes (Dropdown Slots 1 & 2)

The following 29 attributes represent official rules criteria. All 29 appear in alphabetical order in the Attribute dropdowns of Filter Slots 1 & 2. In the right-click Card Attributes menu, any of these attributes that carry a non-empty value on the selected card are displayed in the monospace readout.

Stat Modifiers & Parentheses Notation: Plain values represent direct, unconditional modifiers to the attribute itself (e.g., -1 body or flat armor bonuses). Values enclosed in parentheses (e.g., (1) or (-1)) denote conditional modifiers (such as bonuses restricted to a specific character or class like Warrior only, or temporary combat effects) as well as direct dice roll adjustments (such as +1 to body checks).
Attribute Polarity: Modifiers reflect net impact on the stat total—most notably in Corruption, where character resistance bonuses (e.g. +2 printed on Hobbits) are indexed as negative numbers (-2) because they reduce the character's net corruption burden.

3. Data Provenance & Database Discrepancies

Understanding how card data is modeled and synchronized helps explain unexpected query results, avoid lost edits, and ensure your procedural deck rules remain robust:

A. Cardnum Open Database Synchronization & Modeling Quirks

The catalog synchronizes on application startup from the community-maintained Cardnum repository (cards-dc.json). Because Cardnum was compiled from disparate community databases over many years, several attributes reflect historical database modeling decisions rather than literal transcriptions of printed card text:

  • The Corruption Polarity Inversion (Hobbit Resistance): On character cards, the oval in the lower-right corner displays a bonus to corruption check rolls (for example, Folco Boffin, Merry, Pippin, and Robin Smallburrow all literally display +2, while Frodo displays +4). However, Cardnum unifies the Corruption field across all card types to represent net corruption burden:
    • Items and hazards that inflict corruption points (CP) are positive (e.g. 1, 2, 3 CP).
    • Character resistance bonuses that reduce the risk of corruption are indexed as negative values (e.g. -2 for Hobbits, -4 for Frodo) because mathematically, +2 to the check roll equals -2 to the net corruption burden.
    • To find corruption-resistant characters, filter for negative values like -2 rather than +2.
  • Parenthesized Values: Values in parentheses (such as (1) or (-1)) indicate conditional modifiers (e.g., Warrior only on Valiant Sword, or Éowyn only on Helm of Her Secrecy) or direct dice roll check adjustments (such as +1 to body check rolls on Stabbing Tongue of Fire, indexed as (-1) body).
  • Creature Traits in Skills: Cardnum stores hazard tactical traits (such as Flying, Ringwraith, Undead, or Drake) in the Skill field alongside character classes (Warrior, Scout, etc.).
  • Shorthand Codes: Site cards occasionally feature legacy shorthand classifications, such as B (Border-hold), B F (Border-hold/Free-hold), or Wizardhaven (Fallen-wizard havens from The White Hand).
  • Composite Playable Strings vs. Discrete Item Flags: On physical site cards, playable entries are comma-separated (e.g., "Playable: Information, Items (minor)"). In Cardnum's raw database (cards-dc.json), category commas were omitted, resulting in run-on strings like "Information Items (minor)" or "Scroll of Isildur Palantiri Items (minor, major)".
    • Because the application indexes official attributes directly, each unique permutation appears as a single dropdown item in Filter Slots 1 & 2.
    • Cardnum already decomposed all playability criteria into individual boolean flag attributes: MinorItem, MajorItem, GreaterItem, GoldRing, Information, Palantiri, Scroll, and Hoard.
    • For procedural deck rules and filter searches, query the specific attribute (e.g., "MinorItem": "yes" or "Information": "yes") rather than matching against the composite Playable string.

B. Curated Local Master Dataset & Data Persistence

MECCG Deck Builder ships with a curated, validated master dataset (cards-dc.json) loaded directly from local storage on launch. The application does not contact remote servers on startup, so it will never overwrite your local file.

Any manual corrections or customizations made directly to cards-dc.json persist permanently across sessions and restarts.

C. Recommended Workaround: Custom Categories & Tags

The cleanest, permanent way to handle missing or unintuitive official attributes is to create local taxonomy tags:

  1. Right-click the card and select Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...] (or open Taxonomy > Manage Custom Tags...).
  2. Enter your preferred category and tag (for example, Corruption Resistance: +2, Combat Role: Scout Support, or Skill Fix: Sage).
  3. Filter by these terms using Custom Tags (Slots 3 & 4) in the filter bar.
  4. Back up your assignments at any time via Taxonomy > Save Tag Set... so they can be preserved or shared across machines.

D. Authoring Robust Procedural Deck Rules

Because upstream open databases are maintained by community volunteers and could experience structural updates (or transition to alternative mirrors such as Play MECCG), author your procedural generation JSON templates defensively:

  • Use Semicolon OR Logic: Match multiple related variations where appropriate (e.g., "Skill": "Diplomat; Sage" or "Corruption": "-2; -4").
  • Query Custom Tags When Appropriate: If a strategy relies on roles or classifications that Cardnum represents inconsistently, tag the cards yourself and query your user taxonomy using "Tags": { "Archetype": "Ring Destruction" } instead of relying solely on "Attributes".
  • Always Provide Fallbacks: Attach a nested Fallback rule to any query that depends on specific database strings. If an upstream attribute value shifts, the engine will detect the shortfall and execute the fallback automatically, ensuring your deck remains complete and legal.

Custom Taxonomy & Tag Management

MECCG Deck Builder allows you to classify cards using your own customizable taxonomy system (for example, Strategy → Ring Destruction or Role → Scout Support).

1. Tagging Cards & Rapid Authoring

You can assign, inspect, toggle, or author custom tags through two complementary interfaces:

A. The Card Taxonomy Inspector (Right Pane)

Click [ Card Taxonomy ] at the top of the right pane to open the dedicated metadata inspector. As you arrow or click through cards in the Master List, the inspector updates instantly:

  • Live Monospace Readout: Displays all official rules attributes and assigned custom tags. Long tag lists (such as characters with multiple regions or sites) wrap cleanly under the colon using a column-aligned hanging indent, with smooth vertical mouse-wheel scrolling for dense cards.
  • Filter-Synchronized Category: When you filter by a custom category in bottom Slot 3 (or Slot 4), the Quick Assign Category dropdown automatically mirrors your selection.
  • Status Checkmarks (✓): In the Quick Assign Tag dropdown, any tag currently held by the inspected card is prefixed with a checkmark (✓).
  • Single & Multi-Tag Assignment (+ Assign): Select or type a tag and click + Assign (or press Enter). You can assign multiple tags in one action by separating them with semicolons (e.g. Cardolan; Rhudaur; The Shire).
  • Targeted Removal (- Remove): If the Tag dropdown shows an assigned tag, clicking - Remove strips that specific tag. If the tag field is blank or doesn't match an assigned tag, clicking - Remove opens a popup menu listing all tags currently on the card for quick one-click deletion.
  • Direct Authoring (New Tag...): Opens the tag creation dialog, pre-seeded with the active category and pre-populated with all existing tags, to register and assign a new tag in one step.

B. In-Situ Context Menus (Master List & Deck Tabs)

You can also tag cards directly from any list without switching panes:

  • Assign or Toggle a Tag: Right-click a card and navigate to Assign Tag > [Category] > [Tag]. Currently assigned tags display a checkmark (✓). Clicking an already-assigned tag toggles it off.
  • Author a New Tag on the Fly: Right-click a card and select Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...].
  • Add Tag to Existing Category: Under Assign Tag > [Category], click + Add Tag... to append a new tag value directly into that specific category.
  • Granular Removal: The right-click Remove Tag submenu displays each tag currently assigned to that card, allowing you to remove individual tags without clearing the entire category.
Multi-Tagging: Cards can hold multiple tags within the same category. For example, a multi-role character can hold both Scout Support and Ranger Buffer under the Role category.

2. Taxonomy Manager (Taxonomy > Manage Custom Tags...)

For centralized catalog-wide organization, select Taxonomy > Manage Custom Tags... to open the management dialog:

  • Add Categories: Create new classification categories (e.g. Deck Theme, Hazard Strategy, Role).
  • Add Tags: Add predefined tag values under any selected category so they appear in dropdown filters and context menus.
  • Rename Categories or Tags: Rename terms across your taxonomy; all tagged cards in the catalog are updated automatically.
  • Delete Categories or Tags: Safely remove terms from the database and strip them from all tagged cards.

3. Saving, Loading & Merging Custom Tag Sets

The application differentiates between source files (read-only files pulled into memory) and destination files (files written to disk):

Menu Action File Role Behavior in Active Session (Memory) Effect on Disk
Taxonomy > Load Tag Set... Source Wipe & Replace: Clears all active categories and tags in memory, then loads the selected file fresh. Read-only (file on disk is not modified).
Taxonomy > Merge Tag Set... Source Append & Combine: Reads the selected file and folds its categories and tags into your active memory without erasing what is already open. Read-only (file on disk is not modified).
Taxonomy > Save Tag Set... Destination None (active taxonomy in memory remains unchanged). Write / Export: Serializes all categories and tag assignments currently in memory out to the chosen .json file.
Automatic Baseline Loading: On launch, the application automatically loads Rules_Support_Tags.json (if present in the program folder) as the baseline taxonomy into memory. Because memory is already populated on launch, you never need to load or merge this baseline file manually.

Where to Store Your Tags: Baseline vs. Modular Files

When you author or extract custom tags, choose your storage location based on how you want to use them:

  • Auto-Loaded Baseline: If you want your new tags to be permanently available in every future session, select Taxonomy > Save Tag Set..., select Rules_Support_Tags.json, and confirm overwrite.
  • Modular Strategy Files: If you are creating project-specific tags (such as a private tournament hazard package), save them under a distinct filename (e.g. Hazard_Packages.json). You can merge this file into any session on demand using Taxonomy > Merge Tag Set....

Understanding "Merge Tag Set..." (Worked Example)

Suppose you receive a specialized tag set from another player called Hazard_Packages.json (which tags cards with custom labels like Hazard Strategy: Nazgûl Rush):

  • If you used "Load Tag Set...": The program would wipe out your baseline rules tags (Resolved Site, Faction Bonus) and replace them with the hazard file. The deck generator would no longer know how to resolve starting sites or recruit faction bonuses.
  • When you use "Merge Tag Set...": The program reads Hazard_Packages.json as a source. It keeps all of your existing rules tags and appends the hazard tags right alongside them. If a card already has tags in a category, new tags are safely appended with a semicolon separator (e.g., Orcs; Trolls).

Procedural Deck Generation Engine

MECCG Deck Builder features an automated generation engine that builds legal, randomized decks from declarative JSON rule templates (via Deck > Generate from Rules... [Ctrl+G] or F5).

Core Generation Mechanics

  • Unified Attribute & Tag Querying: Rules can combine any official card attributes (Attributes) and custom user categories (Categories). All criteria must match, with semicolon OR support inside any field and universal wildcard matching (* and All).
  • Deck Copy Limits: Automatically enforces standard card copy limits: maximum 1 copy for unique cards and up to 3 copies for non-unique cards across the entire deck.
  • Maximum Card Variety: When filling multiple card slots from a broad query, the engine prioritizes unused cards before assigning duplicate copies. To include multiple copies of a specific card, query it directly by Name with your desired Count.
  • Randomized Thematic Branches (RandomChoice): Author multiple company themes or hazard packages in a single template, using weighted probability to randomly choose a theme and assign a tailored deck title.
  • Leader & Variable Capture (SaveAs & {...}): Capture chosen characters into named variables (e.g. "SaveAs": "Leader") and query their attributes (e.g. {Leader.Home}) or categories (e.g. {Leader.Category:Faction Bonus}) in subsequent rules.
  • Automated Shortfall Backups (Fallback): Attach secondary backup rules that execute automatically if a primary query yields fewer cards than requested due to uniqueness limits or missing tags.
  • Instant Re-Run (F5): Press F5 (Deck > Re-run Deck Rules) to immediately re-generate fresh randomized variations directly from disk without re-opening file dialogs.
Related Guides: Review the JSON Schema Reference for syntax specifications, or follow the step-by-step Dynamic Factions Worked Example.

Deck Building Operations

Managing Decks via the Deck Menu

  • New Deck (Ctrl+N): Clears all five deck partitions to start fresh.
  • Open Deck... (Ctrl+O): Opens an assembled deck instance from a native JSON save file.
  • Save Deck (Ctrl+S): Saves the current deck instance to disk.
  • Save Deck As...: Saves the deck under a new file title.
  • Export Deck... (Ctrl+E): Exports the deck to Tabletop Simulator, Play MECCG, Cardnum, Archive, or Text format.

Adding Cards

  • Fastest Method: Switch to your desired deck tab on the right, find the card in the Master List, and double-click it. (Note: Double-clicking continues to deposit cards into your active deck partition even when the Card Taxonomy inspector view is currently visible).
  • Drag and Drop: Left-click and drag the card from the Master List onto any visible tab list.
  • Targeted Right-Click: Right-click a card in the Master List, open the Copy submenu, and pick the destination tab (Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, Sites). This automatically switches focus to that tab.

Duplicating Cards

To add another copy of a card already in a deck tab, simply double-click it directly within that tab's list.

Moving Cards Between Tabs

  1. Right-click the card inside any deck tab.
  2. Highlight Move.
  3. Select the destination tab. The card is added to the target tab and removed from the current tab.

Deleting Cards

  • Right-click the card in the deck tab and select Delete.

Deck Rules JSON Schema Reference

Procedural deck generation templates are declarative JSON files loaded via Deck > Generate from Rules... (Ctrl+G, or re-run instantly with F5). This reference details all JSON schema elements, properties, data types, default values, multi-card collections, and token interpolation rules.

1. Root Object (DeckGenerationRuleSet)

Property Type Default Description
DeckTitle string "Generated Deck" Default title assigned to the deck. Can be dynamically overridden by a branch choice at runtime.
RuleSetType string "SequentialRules" Execution strategy identifier (reserved for future execution engines).
Version string "1.0" Schema version indicator.
Rules array of objects [] An ordered list of DeckGenerationRule objects evaluated sequentially from top to bottom.

2. Rule Object (DeckGenerationRule)

Property Type Default Description
RuleType string "FilterQuery" Rule mode:
  • "FilterQuery": Standard query that samples matching cards.
  • "RandomChoice" (or "Choice" / "OneOf" / "Or"): Evaluates a weighted random branch from Choices.
Name string "" Descriptive name displayed in generation logs and shortfall notices.
Section string "Resources" Target deck partition: "Pool", "Resources", "Hazards", "Sideboard", or "Sites".
Count integer 1 The total number of card copies requested by this rule. For broad queries, the engine prioritizes distinct card titles (variety-first) before assigning duplicates; for exact title queries (e.g. {"Name": "Marvels Told"}), it adds multiple copies of that specific card up to legal deck limits.
SaveAs string "" Captures all cards successfully selected by this rule into an in-memory variable (e.g. "Leader" or "ExpeditionSites"). If Count is greater than 1, downstream placeholders ({VariableName.Property}) resolve to a deduplicated, semicolon-delimited union set across all captured cards.
Sets array of strings [] Restricts sampling to specific expansion set codes (e.g. ["METW", "MEDM"]). If omitted, defaults to the sets currently checked in the app's Catalog menu.
Attributes dictionary (Attribute: Value) {} Key-value pairs of official card attributes and required values (e.g. {"Race": "Dwarf", "Skill": "Diplomat"}). Supports semicolon OR syntax and variable interpolation.
Categories dictionary (Category: Tag) {} Key-value pairs of custom taxonomy categories and required tags (e.g. {"Faction Bonus": "Wood-elves", "Automatic Attack": "Dragon"}). Supports semicolon OR syntax and variable interpolation.
Fallback object null A nested DeckGenerationRule executed automatically if this rule fails to fulfill its requested Count (due to missing tags, zero matching candidates, or deck uniqueness limits). Inherits the parent's target Section if unspecified.
Choices array of objects [] Used when RuleType is "RandomChoice". Contains weighted branches.

3. Branch Choice Object (DeckGenerationChoice)

Property Type Default Description
Name string "" Branch label recorded in the execution log (e.g. "Dwarf Company").
DeckTitle string "" Optional deck title override applied if this branch is selected.
Weight integer 1 Relative lottery weight. Selection probability equals Weight / Total Weights (e.g., choices weighted 1 and 3 yield 25% and 75% selection chances).
Rules array of objects [] The list of sub-rules executed sequentially if this branch wins the roll.

4. Query & Placeholder Interpolation Rules

A. Semicolon Multi-Value OR Logic

Any string inside Attributes or Categories can contain multiple semicolon-delimited values. A card matches if it satisfies any of the values: 

"Attributes": {
  "Skill": "Warrior; Scout",
  "Secondary": "Major Item; Minor Item"
},
"Categories": {
  "Automatic Attack": "Dragon; Drake"
}

B. Wildcard & Universal Sentinel Matching (* and All)

Any query criterion in Attributes or Categories that contains * or All acts as a wildcard, satisfying that check for any card that meets the other constraints in the rule. This is particularly valuable when querying properties dynamically captured from character cards: 

"Attributes": {
  "Primary": "Resource",
  "Secondary": "Faction",
  "Name": "{Leader.Category:Faction Bonus}"
}

If the captured leader is a universal diplomat like Adrazar (tagged Faction Bonus: All), the placeholder resolves to "Name": "All". Rather than failing to find a card literally named "All", the engine recognizes the sentinel, treats the Name criterion as an open wildcard, and randomly samples from all faction cards available in your active expansions.

C. Runtime Variable Interpolation (SaveAs → {...})

When a rule captures one or more cards via "SaveAs": "MyVar", downstream rules can dynamically query those cards' properties using bracketed tokens:

Unmet Dependency Handling: If a token references a category or attribute that is absent on the captured card(s), it resolves to an empty string (""). The rule recognizes that the dependency was not met, adds 0 cards, and cleanly hands execution over to the Fallback rule without interrupting generation.

5. Native Save Files (.json) vs. Rule Templates (.json)

Both deck save files and procedural rule sets share the .json extension, but serve distinct roles:

  • Deck Save Files (Deck > Save Deck / Open Deck...): Store an assembled deck instance. Root keys: CurrentDeckTitle, SetList, PoolList, ResourceList, HazardList, SideboardList, and SiteList.
  • Rule Templates (Deck > Generate from Rules...): Declarative instructions used to generate random decks on demand. Root keys: DeckTitle, RuleSetType, and Rules.

Card Artwork Cache & Downloader

Card Artwork Cache System

The application employs a high-performance two-tier caching architecture designed to run reliably in restricted environments (such as C:\Program Files):

  1. Memory Cache: An in-memory cache holding up to 10,000 active Bitmaps for instant display when clicking or navigating.
  2. Local Disk Cache: Checks for card images in the user storage cache under %LOCALAPPDATA%\MECCG Deck Builder\Images\{Set}\ (or local subfolders in portable mode).
    • If found locally in user storage or in pre-bundled application set folders, the image loads immediately with zero network latency.
    • If missing, it downloads asynchronously from Cardnum, saves a copy to disk in user storage, and loads it into memory.

Batch Image Downloader

To pre-cache card artwork for tournament or offline use:

  1. Enable all sets you want cached in the Catalog menu (or choose Catalog > Select All Expansions).
  2. Reset filters (Ctrl+R) so all cards appear in the Master List.
  3. Select Catalog > Download Card Artwork....
Background Download: The batch downloader runs asynchronously with real-time progress reported in the window title bar, keeping the application responsive.

Offline Architecture & Database Upgrades

  • Curated Local Database: The application starts immediately using the local curated card (cards-dc.json) and set (sets-dc.json) definitions with zero startup network calls.
  • Portable Mode: Placing an empty file named portable.flag next to MECCG Deck Builder.exe directs all images, data files, and user settings to stay inside the application folder rather than using %LOCALAPPDATA%.

MECCG Deck Builder is a dedicated Windows desktop application designed to build, organize, filter, and export decks for the Middle-earth Collectible Card Game (MECCG) published by Iron Crown Enterprises (I.C.E.), including official expansions and player council Dreamcard sets.

Key Capabilities

  • Complete Offline Catalog: Launches instantly using a local, validated database of official cards and sets with zero startup latency or network dependency.
  • On-Demand Image Preview & Caching: Displays high-resolution card artwork downloaded on demand and cached locally to conserve bandwidth.
  • Five-Section Deck Partitioning: Organizes cards into standard MECCG deck partitions: Pool, Resources, Hazards, Sideboard, and Sites.
  • Live Card Taxonomy Inspector: Inspect official rules statistics and user taxonomy live in the right pane with column-aligned wrapping, filter synchronization, checkmark status tracking, and a pinned quick-assign toolbar.
  • Dual-Layer Filtering: Filter the card catalog simultaneously by official card attributes (race, skills, items, alignments) and your own customizable user tags.
  • Automated Deck Generator: Build complete, tournament-legal decks from customizable rule templates—featuring natural card variety, branching company themes, dynamic leader recruitment, and automatic backups.
  • Multi-Platform Exporting: Directly export decks to Tabletop Simulator (TTS), Play MECCG online client, Cardnum list format, structured text archives, or plain text lists.
  • Custom Taxonomy & Spreadsheet Tools: Scan card text for traits and abilities, link character homes to geographic regions, and audit or edit custom tags in bulk using Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets.

Companion Rules Tag Set Reference

MECCG Deck Builder utilizes a two-tier database architecture on startup, loading two distinct local files with zero network latency:

  • cards-dc.json (Core Catalog): The official card database containing printed rules statistics (Primary, Alignment, Race, Skills, Mind, Prowess, etc.), originally derived from open Cardnum data with local developer corrections. This file represents the immutable card catalog.
  • Rules_Support_Tags.json (Rules Intelligence Layer): A companion taxonomy dataset authored entirely by the developer. It bridges unstructured card text into queryable taxonomy tags—mapping site automatic attacks, character recruiting bonuses, and home site resolutions so that generic procedural deck rules can generate legal, themed decks automatically.
Pre-Packaged Developer Baseline: All categories, tags, and site resolutions listed in this reference are already completed and pre-packaged. You do not need to run any extractions or tag any cards—the procedural deck generator and filter dropdowns can use these categories immediately upon opening the app.

Where to Store Your Own Custom Tags

If you create your own taxonomy categories or tags using the Tag Manager or Extraction Tools, you have two choices for where to store them:

  • Option 1: Merge into the Auto-Loaded Baseline (Rules_Support_Tags.json): If you want your custom categories to load automatically every time you launch the application, choose Taxonomy > Save Tag Set..., select Rules_Support_Tags.json, and confirm overwrite.
  • Option 2: Save to a Modular Tag File (e.g. Tournament_Hazards.json): If you are creating specialized strategies or sharing tag sets with other players, save them to a standalone .json file. These files will not load automatically on launch; you pull them into your active session on demand via Taxonomy > Load Tag Set... or Taxonomy > Merge Tag Set....

Smart Cascading Filters & Automatic Conflict Resolution

The filter engine uses intelligent cascading logic to ensure you only browse relevant options:

  • Static Keys (Attribute & Category): The upper dropdowns always display all available attributes (Slots 1 & 2) and all taxonomy categories (Slots 3 & 4) across the entire catalog, regardless of which expansion sets are currently checked.
  • Dynamic Value & Tag Pruning: The lower dropdowns (Value and Tag) automatically prune their lists in real time. They only show values and tags present on cards that satisfy your active expansion sets and the criteria in all other active filter slots.
  • Order-Independent Narrowing: You can configure filter slots in any order. For example:
    • Enable only The Wizards (METW) in the Catalog menu.
    • In Slot 1, select Attribute: Primary. On its own, the Value dropdown lists all 5 primary card types (Character, Resource, Hazard, Site, Region).
    • In Slot 2, select Attribute: Skill. On its own, the Value dropdown lists 16 skills.
    • Now choose Value: Diplomat in Slot 2.
    • Slot 1's Value dropdown instantly prunes from 5 options down to just 2: Character and Resource, because in METW only characters and certain resource cards possess the Diplomat skill.
  • Automatic Conflict Resolution (Set Deselection): Because dynamic pruning only offers values and tags that currently match cards, it is impossible to manually select a zero-result combination using the dropdowns. Instead, conflicts only occur when you deselect an expansion set in the Catalog menu. When a set is unchecked, the engine re-evaluates all active slots simultaneously:
    • If a currently selected Value or Tag only existed in the removed set, that slot automatically clears to blank ("") so you are not left viewing an empty list.
    • If the selection still exists in the remaining sets, it remains selected.
    • Example: With both METW and METD checked, Slot 1 set to Primary = Character, and Slot 2 set to Race = Hobbit, unchecking METW causes Slot 2 to automatically clear to blank because METD contains no Hobbit characters (whereas if Slot 2 were set to Race = Dwarf, that selection would remain intact because Dwarves also appear in METD).

CSV Spreadsheet Pipeline

MECCG Deck Builder features a two-way CSV spreadsheet pipeline via the Taxonomy menu (Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)... and Import Taxonomy (CSV)...). This allows you to audit card taxonomy across hundreds of cards at a glance, bulk-assign tags in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, and perform multi-category edits in a single import.

1. Dynamic Spreadsheet Column Layout

When you select Taxonomy > Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)..., the export automatically configures its columns based on your active filter slots:

Column Header Role / Type Description & Behavior
Card Name Required The exact printed title of the card (e.g. Anborn, Adrazar). Matches cards in the catalog.
Set Required The 4-letter expansion code (e.g. METW, MEDM, MEAS). Disambiguates reprints across expansions.
[Active Official Attributes] Reference (Read-Only) Any official rules attributes selected in Slots 1 & 2 (e.g. Race, Skill, Alignment). Populated with each card's official data. Defaults to Primary if no attributes are selected.
Import Safety: All official Cardnum attributes are automatically recognized and skipped during import, ensuring they never become custom tags.
[Custom Category Columns] Editable (Custom Tags) Any custom categories selected in Slots 3 & 4 (e.g. Faction Focus, Combat Role). Exports pre-populated with all tags currently assigned to each card. If no custom category is selected in the filter slots, an [Insert Category Name] template column is generated instead.
Card Text Reference (Read-Only) Full printed rules text for reference while editing. Automatically skipped during import.
Multi-Tagging Syntax: To assign multiple tags within the same category column, separate them with a semicolon (;), for example: Dwarf Factions; All Factions or Scout Support; Ranger Buffer.

2. Authoritative "Edit & Replace" Import Behavior

When you select Taxonomy > Import Taxonomy (CSV)..., the importer treats the spreadsheet as the authoritative record for every custom category column included in the file:

  • Multiple Columns Processed Simultaneously: You can add as many custom category columns side-by-side as you like (e.g. Faction Focus, Role, Hazard Package, Deck Priority). The importer evaluates every custom column for every card in the spreadsheet.
  • Full Edit & Replace (Not Append): If a card already possesses tags in a category, the import replaces them with the exact contents of the cell. If you change Scout Support to Warrior Tank, the old tag is removed and the new tag is assigned.
  • Clearing & Deleting Tags: Emptying a cell (or typing [clear], [none], or -) completely removes that category's tags from that card.
  • Column Scope Isolation: Only the custom categories present as headers in the CSV are updated. Any categories not in the spreadsheet remain completely untouched.
  • Card Scope Isolation: The import only updates the specific cards listed in the CSV. Any cards from your catalog omitted from the file retain their existing tags.
  • Placeholder Protection: Unmodified template headers (like [Insert Category Name]) and instructional cell hints (like [Insert tag...]) are automatically detected and ignored.

3. Step-by-Step Workflow

Scenario A: Auditing & Editing Existing Tags

  1. In the main window, choose the expansion sets you want to audit in the Catalog menu.
  2. In Slot 3 (bottom panel), select the category you want to inspect (e.g. Category: Faction Focus).
  3. Select Taxonomy > Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)... and save the file.
  4. Open the CSV in Excel or Google Sheets. The Faction Focus column is already filled with all current tags. You can glance down the column, correct typos, delete tags, or add second tags with a semicolon (;).
  5. Save the spreadsheet as a CSV file.
  6. In MECCG Deck Builder, select Taxonomy > Import Taxonomy (CSV)... and select your edited file. Your catalog is updated instantly.

Scenario B: Drafting Brand New Categories from Scratch

  1. Filter the Master List to the cards you want to classify (for example, set Slot 1 to Primary = Character).
  2. Select Taxonomy > Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)....
  3. Open the file in your spreadsheet editor. Replace the header [Insert Category Name] with your desired category name (e.g. Combat Role).
  4. (Optional) Add additional custom category columns next to it (e.g. Expedition Priority).
  5. Enter tags for each card and save as CSV.
  6. Select Taxonomy > Import Taxonomy (CSV).... All new categories and tags are immediately registered in the application.

Located under Taxonomy > Extract Tags with Rules..., this dialog provides automated classification tools scoped strictly to the cards currently visible in your Master List. Pre-Packaged Baseline Notice: The extraction workflows demonstrated below (such as tagging Dark-holds, scanning faction recruiting bonuses, and mapping home regions) represent the exact automated methods the developer used to build Rules_Support_Tags.json. Because these tags are already shipped with the software, you do not need to run these extractions yourself before building decks—they are documented here so you can inspect the methodology and apply it to your own custom classifications.
Master List Scoping: All extraction tools evaluate only the cards currently visible in the Master List. To target specific cards (e.g. only characters or only cards from a specific expansion), set your filters in the main window before opening the dialog.

Scan Card Text for Catalog Entities

Scans the gameplay rules text of cards in scope for references to published catalog cards (such as factions, regions, or character names):

  • Target Entity: Select the official attribute and value that defines the catalog cards you want to search for (e.g. Secondary = Faction or Primary = Region). The engine inspects all active sets and gathers all published titles (e.g. Wood-elves, Riders of Rohan).
  • Save to Category: Enter the custom category where matching tags will be stored (e.g. Faction Bonus).
  • Flavor Text Protection: All Tolkien book quotes (enclosed in quotation marks) and book citations (e.g. —LotRI) are automatically stripped before evaluation, ensuring lore quotes never generate false tags.

Worked Example: Extracting Faction Recruiting Bonuses

Many characters have rules text conferring Direct Influence bonuses when recruiting specific factions (e.g. Thranduil → Wood-elves, Dáin II → Iron Hill Dwarves). We can scan the text of all characters across the catalog and tag them with their recruitable factions automatically:

  1. Scope the Master List: In the main window, check your active expansions in the Catalog menu. In Filter Slot 1, set Attribute: Primary and Value: Character so only character cards are evaluated.
  2. Configure the Scanner: Open Taxonomy > Extract Tags with Rules..., choose Scan Card Text for Catalog Entities, and enter:
    • Target Entity: Secondary = Faction
    • Save to Category: Faction Bonus
  3. Preview and Apply: Click Test / Preview Matches to inspect all characters whose gameplay text references a published faction title. Click Apply Tags to Catalog, then persist your tags via Taxonomy > Save Tag Set... overwriting Rules_Support_Tags.json.

Cross-Card Attribute Lookup

Cross-references an attribute on cards in scope (such as a character's Home) against related destination cards across the catalog (such as a Site) to pull in a secondary attribute (such as Region) as a custom tag:

  • Read Attribute: The attribute on cards currently in scope used to match the destination card (e.g. Character Home).
  • Lookup Entity: The catalog criteria used to identify the target cards (e.g. Primary = Site).
  • Extract Attribute: The official attribute pulled from the matched cards (e.g. Site Region).
  • Save to Category: The custom category where the extracted tag will be saved (e.g. Home Region).
Compound Name Handling: Characters with multiple locations (e.g. Rivendell, Bree) automatically resolve each site individually to generate clean, semicolon-delimited multi-tags (Arthedain; Rhudaur).

Worked Example: Mapping Character Homes to Geographic Regions

Character cards list home sites (e.g. Aragorn II → Rivendell, Boromir → Minas Tirith, Théoden → Edoras), but lack geographic region attributes. To enable regional company recruitment rules without manual tagging:

  1. Scope the Master List: In the main window, check your active expansions in the Catalog menu, and set Filter Slot 1: Attribute: Primary, Value: Character.
  2. Configure the Lookup: Open Taxonomy > Extract Tags with Rules..., choose Cross-Card Attribute Lookup, and enter:
    • Read Attribute: Home
    • Lookup Entity: Primary = Site
    • Extract Attribute: Region
    • Save to Category: Home Region
  3. Preview and Apply: Click Test / Preview Matches. The engine looks up each character's home site and extracts its region (e.g. Rivendell → Rhudaur, Minas Tirith → Anórien, Edoras → Rohan). Click Apply Tags to Catalog and save via Taxonomy > Save Tag Set....

Custom Pattern Search (Regex)

Searches card rules text using custom .NET regular expressions:

  • Pattern: The text pattern evaluated against card rules text (e.g. Ruins & Lairs in a Wilderness or \b(greater)\b). Case-insensitivity is enabled by default.
  • Assigned Tag: The tag applied to matching cards. Supports three formats:
    • Fixed Text: A single fixed tag (e.g. Cancellation).
    • Multi-Tag List: A semicolon-delimited string (e.g. Barad-dûr; Carn Dûm; Cirith Gorgor).
    • Capture Group ($1): If your pattern contains parentheses (...), using $1 dynamically assigns the exact captured word or phrase.
  • Save to Category: The custom taxonomy category where assigned tags will be stored.
Session Persistence: Your last-used Pattern, Assigned Tag, and Category are automatically remembered across application launches so you can make iterative passes without retyping.

In The Lidless Eye, 15 Minion Orcs, Trolls, and Half-orcs (such as Doeth, Orc Captain, and Troll Lout) have the non-specific home rule Home Site: Any Dark-hold. To allow procedural deck rules to recruit these characters and automatically assign them a valid starting site (via {Leader.Category:Resolved Site}), we can batch-tag all 15 characters in under 30 seconds:

  2. Configure the Pattern Search: Open Taxonomy > Extract Tags with Rules..., choose Custom Pattern Search (Regex), and enter:
    • Pattern: Any Dark-hold
    • Assigned Tag: Barad-dûr; Carn Dûm; Cirith Gorgor; Cirith Ungol; Dol Guldur; Minas Morgul; Urlurtsu Nurn

Batch Rules from File (.json)

For large-scale taxonomy extraction across multiple expansions, you can author batch extraction rule files (.json) containing arrays of compiled regex rules and execute them in a single operation.

Batch Rule Schema

Property Type Description
Category string The custom taxonomy category where matches will be saved (e.g. "Automatic Attack").
Pattern string The .NET regular expression to evaluate against card rules text. Backslashes must be double-escaped for JSON encoding (e.g. "\\b", "\\s+").
TagTemplate string The tag assigned upon match. Can be a fixed string (e.g. "Dwarves") or a capture group token (e.g. "$1").

Worked Example: Sandboxed Site Automatic Attacks

The Goal: We want to classify all site cards across our expansions by the guardian creature species printed in their automatic attack (tagging them as Dragon, Orcs, Trolls, Undead, or Dwarves under the custom category Automatic Attack).

The Challenge: Site cards print automatic attacks in the middle of their rules box, between surface entrances at the top and special site rules at the bottom. A simple text search for creature names causes two distinct false matches:

  1. Top False Matches (Adjacent Sites / Havens): Under-deeps sites list surface entrances at the very top. For example, The Drowning-deeps begins with Adjacent Sites: Blue Mountain Dwarf-hold (13)..., triggering a false Dwarves tag even though its actual attack is a Drake.
  2. Bottom False Matches (Special Rules): Many sites list special racial bonuses or movement effects at the bottom. For example, a site guarded only by Orcs might conclude with Special: Dwarven characters receive +1 direct influence here, triggering an unwanted Dwarves tag.
Building a Two-Sided Search Sandbox:

To isolate only the true automatic attack, we use a tempered regex pattern that starts at the attack header and stops before the special text:

(?is)Automatic-attacks?(?:(?!Special:).)*?\bdwar(?:f|ves)\b
  • (?is)Automatic-attacks?: The Top Guard. Anchors to the attack header, ignoring all site names in Adjacent Sites: or Nearest Haven: above it.
  • (?:(?!Special:).)*?: The Bottom Guard. Advances across lines character-by-character, strictly verifying that it has not reached Special:.
  • \bdwar(?:f|ves)\b: Matches the creature species. If Special: is encountered before the creature name, the match fails immediately.

1. Sample Sandboxed Rule File (Automatic_Attack_Rules.json)

[
  {
    "Category": "Automatic Attack",
    "Pattern": "(?is)Automatic-attacks?(?:(?!Special:).)*?\\bdwar(?:f|ves)\\b",
    "TagTemplate": "Dwarves"
  },
  {
    "Category": "Automatic Attack",
    "Pattern": "(?is)Automatic-attacks?(?:(?!Special:).)*?\\bdrakes?\\b",
    "TagTemplate": "Drake"
  },
  {
    "Category": "Automatic Attack",
    "Pattern": "(?is)Automatic-attacks?(?:(?!Special:).)*?\\borcs?\\b",
    "TagTemplate": "Orcs"
  },
  {
    "Category": "Automatic Attack",
    "Pattern": "(?is)Automatic-attacks?(?:(?!Special:).)*?\\btrolls?\\b",
    "TagTemplate": "Trolls"
  },
  {
    "Category": "Automatic Attack",
    "Pattern": "(?is)Automatic-attacks?(?:(?!Special:).)*?\\b(?:undead|wights?|ghosts?)\\b",
    "TagTemplate": "Undead"
  }
]

2. Step-by-Step Batch Execution & Audit Workflow

  1. Scope the Master List: In the top Catalog menu, check your target expansions (e.g. The Dragons, Dark Minions, The Lidless Eye). In Filter Slot 1, set Attribute: Primary and Value: Site so only site cards are evaluated.
  2. Load and Run the Batch File: Open Taxonomy > Extract Tags with Rules..., select Batch Rules from File (.json), browse to Automatic_Attack_Rules.json, and click Test / Preview Matches. Review the preview list, then click Apply Tags to Catalog.
  3. Audit via CSV Spreadsheet Pipeline: In the main window, set Slot 3: Category: Automatic Attack and select Taxonomy > Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)....
  4. Review in Excel or Google Sheets: Open the CSV to glance down the pre-populated Automatic Attack column. Multi-attack sites (like Carn Dûm or Moria) cleanly show multiple tags (Orcs; Trolls), and complex edge cases can be edited directly in the spreadsheet.
  5. Sync and Persist: Save the CSV and choose Taxonomy > Import Taxonomy (CSV)... to apply your edits. Finally, select Taxonomy > Save Tag Set..., choose Rules_Support_Tags.json, and confirm overwrite so all tags persist permanently across application launches.

Worked Example: Dynamic Faction Recruitment

This end-to-end tutorial demonstrates how to build context-aware procedural deck generation templates using branching company themes, variable capture, dynamic placeholders, and automated shortfall fallbacks.

1. The Goal: Context-Aware Company Themes

In MECCG, leaders often possess direct influence (DI) bonuses against specific factions (for example, Thranduil receives +2 DI against the Wood-elves, and Dáin II receives +2 DI against the Iron Hill Dwarves).

We want to create an automated deck rule template that:

  1. Randomly selects a company theme (e.g. Dwarf Company vs. Elf Company).
  2. Selects an appropriate starting diplomat leader for that company and captures them into an in-memory variable ("SaveAs": "Leader").
  3. Dynamically recruits the specific faction our leader specializes in influencing by matching the card's title to the leader's tagged bonus ("Name": "{Leader.Category:Faction Bonus}").
  4. Gracefully falls back: If the randomly chosen leader has no specific faction bonus (e.g. Balin), the generator must detect the shortfall and automatically fall back to recruiting any faction matching that leader's race ("Race": "{Leader.Race}").

The fallback resolves Race: Dwarf and recruits a generic faction (such as Blue Mountain Dwarves).

# Coding Standards & Guidelines: MECCG Deck Builder
## 1. General Principles - Modern .NET Standard: Target C# 12 / .NET 8 idioms (collection expressions [], pattern matching, nullability annotations). - Separation of Concerns: Keep UI presentation (Form1.cs) strictly separated from domain logic, file I/O, network access, and deck generation algorithms. Forms should act as views, delegating logic to dedicated services or models. - Fail-Safe & User-Friendly: Catch exceptions gracefully, report actionable messages to the user, and never let unhandled background exceptions crash the UI thread.
---
## 2. Naming Conventions
### Identifiers - Classes, Records, Enums, Structs, Methods, Properties: Use PascalCase. - Examples: CardCatalog, GenerateDeck(), DeckTitle - Local Variables, Method Parameters, Private Fields: Use camelCase. - Examples: cardIndex, selectedSet, filePath - Private / Internal Class Fields: Prefix with an underscore _ or use standard camelCase. - Examples: _cards, _httpClient (or cards, s_httpClient for static instances). - Constants: Use PascalCase. - Examples: CardnumCardsUrl, PoolFileSuffix (avoid ALL_CAPS). - Event Handlers in WinForms: Use ControlName_EventName in PascalCase. - Examples: ContentsToolStripMenuItem_Click, ListBoxMaster_SelectedIndexChanged - Note: Ensure the control name starts with an uppercase letter to satisfy Roslyn rule IDE1006.
---
## 3. Architecture & Domain Modeling
### Strongly-Typed Models over Raw Arrays - No More string[] for Entities: Replace List<string[]> and SortedDictionary<string, string> with strongly-typed records or classes (e.g., Card, DeckCard, DeckSection). - Enums for Domain Constants: Use strongly-typed enums for fixed concepts (e.g., DeckSection.Pool, DeckSection.Resources, CardAlignment.Hero). - Immutability Where Appropriate: Card catalog definitions should be read-only once loaded into memory.
### Headless & Testable Domain Logic - Deck export routines, deck import routines, card filtering, and the future procedural deck generator must never take ListBox, ComboBox, or Form controls as parameters. - Operate on pure domain structures (e.g., Deck, IEnumerable<Card>, FilterCriteria) so they can be tested via unit tests and run headless.
---
## 4. Asynchronous Programming & Threading
### No Blocking on Async Tasks - Never use .Result, .Wait(), or .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on the UI thread. - All network requests (HttpClient) and disk I/O should use async / await: - Avoid: string json = s_httpClient.GetStringAsync(url).Result; - Prefer: string json = await s_httpClient.GetStringAsync(url); - Long-running batch operations (such as Download Images or Generate Deck) must be performed asynchronously or on a background task (Task.Run) with progress updates via IProgress<T> or Progress<int>.
---
## 5. Resource Management & GDI+ Safety
### Safe Image Loading (No File Locking) - Never instantiate new Bitmap(filePath) directly for files that might be overwritten or deleted, as GDI+ keeps the file locked indefinitely. - Instead, read the image bytes into a MemoryStream and create an independent Bitmap clone: - Read bytes via File.ReadAllBytes(filePath) - Copy into MemoryStream - Construct Bitmap from stream and return an independent instance.
### Disposal of GDI+ Objects - When assigning a new image to PictureBox.Image, always dispose of the previous image if it is an unmanaged, uncached copy to prevent GDI object leaks. - Always dispose Graphics, Pen, Brush, and Font objects using using statements.
---
## 6. Encodings & String Formats
- Internal Strings: Standard .NET UTF-16 strings. - JSON Serialization: Use UTF-8 without BOM (System.Text.Json or Newtonsoft.Json). - Legacy Play MECCG Files (.play): Explicitly specify Windows-1252 ANSI: - Encoding.GetEncoding(1252) - HTML Help Files (.hhp, .hhc, .hhk): Must be saved as ANSI (Windows-1252) or UTF-8 without BOM/signature. Never save help project files with a UTF-8 BOM.
---
## 7. Error Handling & Defensive Coding
- No Silent Exception Swallowing: Avoid empty catch (Exception) { } blocks. At minimum, log the error or provide user feedback via a status bar or message box. - Specific Exception Catching: Catch specific exceptions (e.g., HttpRequestException, JsonException, IOException) before general Exception. - Collection Key Safety: Use TryGetValue() or ContainsKey() before accessing dictionaries to prevent KeyNotFoundException.
---
## 8. Formatting & Tooling - Indentation: 4 spaces (no tabs in C# source files; tabs permitted only in generated export templates if required by format specification like Tabletop Simulator JSON). - Line Endings: CRLF (\r\n) for Windows compatibility. - Warnings as Errors: Aim for zero compiler warnings and zero Roslyn analyzer warnings on Release builds.

Author tags via the dedicated Manage Custom Tags dialog or right-click Assign Tag > [+ Author New Tag...] without disturbing active filter criteria. - Multi-Platform Export Formats: - Tabletop Simulator (.json): Generates ready-to-use deck files compatible with TTS MECCG mods. - Play MECCG (.play & .playPBEM): Native format for online play. - Cardnum Deck (.cnum): Standard 1 <Code> listing format. - Archive Breakdown (.archive): Categorized breakdown (Items, Events, Characters by race, Sites by type). - Plain Text (.txt): Formatted deck listing. - Procedural Deck Generator: Generate complete decks from JSON rule templates with attribute and category queries, deck copy limits, tiered variety-first duplication, and randomized thematic branches (RandomChoice). Features runtime variable capture (SaveAs), dynamic cross-card property placeholders (e.g. {Leader.Category:Faction Bonus}, {Leader.Home}), universal wildcard sentinels (* and All), multi-card union sets, and automated shortfall fallbacks (Fallback). Re-run instant variations with F5 or load rules via Deck > Generate from Rules... (Ctrl+G). - Automated Taxonomy Extraction: Scan card rules text for catalog entities, perform cross-card attribute lookups, or execute custom regular expressions in an expanded workspace with automatic session persistence via Taxonomy > Extract Tags with Rules.... - Two-Way CSV Spreadsheet Pipeline: Bulk audit and edit catalog taxonomy using Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets with authoritative edit-and-replace synchronization via Taxonomy > Export Taxonomy Draft (CSV)... and Taxonomy > Import Taxonomy (CSV).... - Session Persistence: Remembers your active expansion set selection across application restarts and preserves your last-used taxonomy extraction mode, regular expressions, and tag categories for iterative tagging workflows.
